analysis: The closest option connects programming, logical reasoning, linear algebra and statistics with robotics, computer vision, perception and decision-making. Robotics and the newly selected Linear Systems contribute kinematics, control and signal analysis, while psychology and philosophy supply a complementary account of human cognition. The core supplies neural networks, optimisation and reinforcement learning. These subjects do not reproduce dedicated natural language processing or brain modelling.

The computational option gives additional weight to operating systems, software development, advanced algorithms, numerical methods and advanced calculus. Technical courses support model implementation, evaluation and control. AI Ethics addresses fairness and accountability. The AI and business course supplies an application and organisational context without implying an extra technical AI sequence. Removing the cognitive and advanced psychology courses also resolves their unmet brain-and-behaviour prerequisites.

The cognition option keeps neurobiology, sensory processing, higher cognition, psycholinguistics, development and philosophy of mind. Research design and evidence synthesis support interpretation of human research. Linear algebra and computer vision give a stronger computational link than psychopathology and youth extremism. Neural networks, probabilistic decisions and image processing complement the biological and human topics without equating machine learning and neuroscience.

The three plans differ by 45, 52.5 and 90 EC each way. Offering conflicts are repaired and gateway requirements hold. The dedicated brain-modelling, biologically inspired neural computation and computational linguistics courses remain visible gaps. Groningen expressly distinguishes Neural Computation from deep learning, and the UCR optional research element is separate from the required bachelor project.
constructionStop: Three coherent, distinct options reach the programme limit.

HCBCOGN312.contribution: studies the cognitive and neurobiological mechanisms of language
HCBCOGN312.topics: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
